title: Multi-modal framework for battery state of health evaluation using open-source electric vehicle data
datasets: Own open-source EV field data (released with paper; 3 vehicle types / fleet)
inputs: Partial multi-stage CC charge segment 3.9-4.05 V: charge-capacity sequence, temperature sequence, 2D cell-voltage map, 15 HI points
evidence: split: "we randomly split the samples into the training and testing sets" (Results)
notes: Partial charge window only (3.9-4.05 V); labels via Ah integration + OCV-SOC correction from field charging; HI-point normalization scope not stated; RFR baseline (on HI points) under same random split. Random sample-level split mixes vehicles.

title: Offline and Online Blended Machine Learning for Lithium-Ion Battery Health State Estimation
datasets: Oxford Battery Degradation Dataset; real-world EV/bus data (not public)
inputs: IC peak value (point C) from C/25 pseudo-OCV charge characterization
evidence: P2c: "IC value of peak point C" from "C/25 constant current in the characterization" (Sec. III)
notes: Judgment call: P2c=yes only because the IC curve is from a full slow CC charge (protocol literal); the feature itself is a LOCAL IC peak, not capacity-equivalent [P2c_basis=IC_local]. Offline models from other cells + online adaptation using early target-cell data.

title: A simple feature extraction method for estimating the whole life cycle state of health of lithium-ion batteries using transformer-based neural network
datasets: Cambridge EIS dataset (Zhang et al. 2020, Eunicell LR2032)
inputs: 5 selected EIS points (10 dims: Re/Im) from impedance spectrum
notes: Train 5 cells / val 1 / test 1 (single test cell at 35 C). Baselines are RNN/GRU/LSTM only. Accepted manuscript (pure.ulster.ac.uk).

title: State of Health Estimation for Lithium-Ion Batteries Under Arbitrary Usage Using Data-Driven Multimodel Fusion
datasets: Sandia National Laboratories (SNL) NMC & NCA cycling data
inputs: Scenario-dependent charging features: IC peak & position, CC charging time tcc, CV current slope, voltage-window slope/time, energy, temperatures, SoC0; GPR/BRR/RFR/DeNN + KF fusion
evidence: P2c: features incl. "The time spent during CC charging stage"; "S1: Complete CC-CV charging from 0% SoC to 100%" (Sec. III)
notes: P2c=yes applies to scenario S1 (full charge from 0% SOC incl. tcc); S2-S5 are partial charges. S1-2 report the lowest errors (within +/-2.5%). Bayesian ridge and RFR reported as individual models. Train/test split of cells not stated (5-fold CV for tuning). Preprint version from research.chalmers.se.

title: Domain knowledge-guided machine learning framework for state of health estimation in Lithium-ion batteries
datasets: Stanford UDDS EV-profile aging dataset (Pozzato et al. 2022), 5 NMC cells
inputs: Incremental (minus first-cycle value) power autocorrelation, resistance, charging impedance, energy in charge window 3.6-3.9 V, energy in UDDS discharge window 3.85-3.4 V; linear regression
notes: Partial voltage windows only. Features referenced to first aging cycle (past info, not whole-life -> P3=no). Scenario 2: "LRM is trained using data from all cells except the test cell". Main model is itself linear regression (counted as simple baseline). Text from arXiv html 2409.14575.

title: Graph neural network-based lithium-ion battery state of health estimation using partial discharging curve
datasets: MIT/Severson (Toyota) dataset, 4 LFP cells
inputs: Partial 4C discharge-voltage segment chosen by Matrix Profile (length L1/4-L1/2 of first-cycle discharge) linked into graph with early-cycle segments; GCN
notes: Train first 70% of cycles (from cycle 101), test remaining 30% of the SAME cells. Comparisons only vs other DL methods. arXiv html 2409.00141.

title: Transfer-Learning-Based State-of-Health Estimation for Lithium-Ion Battery With Cycle Synchronization
datasets: MIT/Severson (Toyota) LFP dataset
inputs: Full 4C CC discharge voltage time series synchronized by DTW (warping path to end of discharge), canonical variates -> GRU; transfer learning source->target
evidence: P2: "discharging time step, which is strongly associated with the battery's SOH status" (Sec. III)
notes: DTW warping path spans whole discharge (ends at (m,n), n = target discharge length) -> encodes discharge duration = Q/I under 4C CC. Target-cell early cycles (e.g., first 100) used to train residual model, later cycles of same cell tested. arXiv html 2208.11204.

title: State of Health Estimation of Lithium Iron Phosphate Batteries Based on Degradation Knowledge Transfer Learning
datasets: Sandia National Laboratories LFP (18650) cycling data; synthetic LFP curves (alawa-style simulation)
inputs: Charging voltage/current curves -> degradation-mode (DM) estimates via deepCoral transfer from synthetic data; DMs + charging feature curves + noise -> conditional TS-GAN for SOH
notes: Text does not state the voltage/SOC window of the charging curves used as input (Sandia LFP cycles include full-range charges at 0.5C) -> P2c unclear. LASSO and ARIMA reported as comparison methods. Cell-level train/test split not stated. Accepted version from opus.lib.uts.edu.au.

title: A Joint Estimation Method for the SOC and SOH of Lithium-Ion Batteries Based on AR-ECM and Data-Driven Model Fusion
datasets: University of Michigan Battery Lab (UMBL) dataset; McMaster LG HG2 (SOC only)
inputs: Features from CC charge in 3.53-3.81 V window (segment voltage, dQ/dV peak, normalized equal-voltage-rise time/charge relative to period 1) + past n=30 SOH values in sliding window; HKELM; fused with AR-ECM via EKF
notes: Partial charge window. Note: model input also includes SOH labels of the previous n cycles (sliding-window autoregression) -> not a proxy per protocol but a separate label-history dependence. Normalization is relative to the first period (past info).

title: A Novel Method for Estimating the State of Health of Lithium-Ion Batteries Based on Physics-Informed Neural Network
datasets: XJTU battery dataset (CC discharge batch); Oxford Battery Degradation Dataset
inputs: Health factors: CC-charge equal-voltage-rise time & charge (CTEVI, CCEVI), discharge time and capacity from 3.7 V to end of discharge (DTEVD, DCEVD), IC peak/area (ICPA, ICA); BPNN-based PINN with monotonicity constraints
evidence: P2: "the time from 3.7 V to the end of discharge" (DTEVD) (Sec. 2.2)
notes: DTEVD/DCEVD run to the discharge cutoff (2.5 V) under CC discharge for XJTU -> capacity-equivalent portion of discharge. Split: each battery's cycles divided 6:4 into train/test; transfer-learning experiments train on a source battery and fine-tune on target. Only BPNN as comparison.

title: Physics-informed neural network for lithium-ion battery degradation stable modeling and prognosis
datasets: XJTU (own, released), TJU (Zhu 2022), HUST (Ma 2022), MIT/Severson
inputs: 16 statistical features (mean, std, kurtosis, skewness, charging time, accumulated charge, slope, entropy) from CC voltage window [Vend-0.2, Vend] and CV current 0.5-0.1 A, plus cycle index; PINN
evidence: P3 text: "min-max normalization is performed on the features" (SOH estimation); code dataloader.read_one_csv normalizes each battery file over its whole life
notes: Text alone is ambiguous on normalization scope; public code (github wang-fujin/PINN4SOH, dataloader.py read_one_csv) applies min-max/z-score per battery CSV over all cycles, including the inserted 'cycle index' column -> per-cell whole-life normalization (cycle index becomes life fraction). Coded P3=yes on code evidence (flag as judgment call). Accumulated charge is only over the last 0.2 V + CV tail -> P1=no. Comparisons: MLP, CNN only. Split: "train the model with data from battery A and test it on battery B".

title: A Meta-Learning Method for Few-Shot Multidomain State-of-Health Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries
datasets: Tongji University (TJU, Zhu et al. 2022) NCA and NCM cells
inputs: 10 relaxation-voltage (RV) points from 20-min rest after full charge, Z-score standardized; CNN-attention parallel network with meta-learning
notes: Relaxation features (Zhu 2022 style), not proxies. Z-score scope not stated. Target-domain fine-tuning uses a few samples from the first target cell; "remaining target samples for validation" includes the rest of that cell -> coded within_cell. Comparisons only vs DL models. Accepted manuscript (pure.hud.ac.uk).

title: State of Health Estimation for Lithium-Ion Battery Using Partial Incremental Capacity Curve and Transfer Learning
datasets: Tongji University (TJU) NCA (Dataset 1) and NCM (Dataset 2)
inputs: Partial IC curve values in 3.6-3.8 V during CC charge; stacked BiGRU + transfer learning
notes: Partial window only (main model); an ablation compares against IC over the entire charging process. Pre-training split by cells (stratified ~4:1, 52 training cells). XGBoost and SVR comparisons on IC statistics.

title: Online State-of-Health Estimation for Fast-Charging Lithium-Ion Batteries Based on a Transformer–Long Short-Term Memory Neural Network
datasets: Cambridge coin-cell cycling dataset (public, Dataset 2); proprietary NCM dataset (Dataset 1)
inputs: Times spent in equal voltage sub-intervals of the charging curve (3.4-4.2 V for Dataset 1; 3.7-4.2 V for Cambridge), sliding window; Transformer-LSTM
evidence: P2c: "a voltage range from 3.4 V to 4.2 V was chosen as the overall …" (Sec. 2.2)
notes: Judgment call: sum of interval times = CC charge time over 3.4-4.2 V; cells discharged to 2.5 V so 3.4 V is near charge start -> coded yes (proprietary Dataset 1). For the public Cambridge dataset window is 3.7-4.2 V (partial; ends at charge cutoff). Data min-max normalized (scope not stated). Comparisons GRU/LSTM/Transformer only.

title: State of Health Estimation Procedure for Lithium-Ion Batteries Using Partial Discharge Data and Support Vector Regression
datasets: MIT/Severson (Toyota) 124 LFP cells
inputs: 3 features from discharge capacity curves Q(V) (difference vs cycle-10 reference curve, area/energy-type features) over full 2.0-3.4 V interval and partial intervals, plus temperature; SVR
evidence: P2: "full discharge capacity curves, built from the full interval of 2 to 3.4 V" (Abstract)
notes: Headline result (mean test R2 0.962) uses full-interval Q(V); partial intervals also evaluated. Features referenced to cycle 10 (past info). Normalized cycle number used only for visualization. 15 random test cells, 109 train. No linear/tree baseline.

title: Machine Learning-Based State-of-Health Estimation of Battery Management Systems Using Experimental and Simulation Data
datasets: XJTU battery dataset (batch 5 strategy); AnyLogic synthetic data
inputs: 4-channel time series (voltage, current, temperature, SoC) of 128 time steps, min-max scaled to [-1,1]; MLP and LSTM
notes: Methods do not state which segment of the cycle the 128-step window covers, how SoC is obtained, the normalization scope, or the train/test split of real cells. MLP described as baseline (not linear/tree).

title: A deep learning approach for state-of-health estimation of lithium-ion batteries based on differential thermal voltammetry and attention mechanism
datasets: Oxford Battery Degradation Dataset 1 (cells 1,3,4,7,8)
inputs: Peak/valley features (FV1, FV3, FV6) of differential thermal voltammetry (DTV) curves; LSTM with attention
notes: Text does not state whether DTV curves come from the 1C characterization charge or discharge (both full-range in Oxford data) -> P2/P2c unclear; features are local peaks/valleys. Both train/test proportion (within-cell) and leave-one-battery-out CV reported; coded cell_held_out because LOO results are reported.

title: State of Health Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries Using a Multi-Feature-Extraction Strategy and PSO-NARXNN
datasets: Oxford Battery Degradation Dataset 1
inputs: 8 HFs: CC-charge time and charge in 3.8-4.0 V (T1, Q1), differential-temperature (DT) peaks/valleys, IC features from CC charge; PSO-NARX NN (input delay 1, feedback delay 2)
evidence: P2c: DT curve "first undergoes a period of rapid ascent, reaching its first peak value" (Sec. 2.2.2)
notes: Judgment call: P2c=yes only in the literal protocol sense (DT/IC features taken from the full CC charge curve, which in Oxford starts from the discharged state); features are LOCAL peaks [P2c_basis=DT/IC_local], while capacity-type features use 3.8-4.0 V only. NARX feeds back previous SOH outputs. Train on 1 cell, test on 7.

title: Reducing the Computational Cost for Artificial Intelligence-Based Battery State-of-Health Estimation in Charging Events
datasets: Sandia National Laboratories (NMC cell, 0-100% SOC, 0.5C CCCV charge)
inputs: Charging time series of voltage, current, charged capacity (Ah, in time) and temperature over a chosen SOC window of the CCCV charge (from full charge down to 60-100% SOC window); Bi-LSTM
evidence: P1: features include "charged capacity in time (Ah)" (Sec. 2.2); charge spans 0-100% SOC
notes: Window-length study starts from the full 0-100% charge; final recommended input is 60-100% SOC window (CV phase). Whether the charged-capacity channel is re-zeroed at the window start is not stated (if cumulative, it remains capacity-equivalent). Cycles randomly divided into train/validation/test (single test-condition cell) -> within_cell.

title: State-of-health estimation for lithium-ion batteries based on Bi-LSTM-AM and LLE feature extraction
datasets: Oxford Battery Degradation Dataset 1 (cells 1,3,4,7,8)
inputs: Whole-cycle DTV data interpolated to equal length, reduced by LLE (vs PCA/SVD); Bi-LSTM with attention
notes: Whole DTV curve per cycle is used, but text does not say whether from the charge or discharge characterization -> P2/P2c unclear (if full-curve, the DTV vector spans the whole curve). 50/50 split of each battery's cycles. LLE fit scope not stated.

title: Early Prediction of the Health Conditions for Battery Cathodes Assisted by the Fusion of Feature Signal Analysis and Deep-Learning Techniques
datasets: Oxford Battery Degradation Dataset 1 (cells 1,3,4,7,8)
inputs: Singular values of the DTV vector and DTV peak/valley features from CC charging, 20 s sampling; LSTM on feature time series (joint SOH/RUL)
evidence: P2c: "singular values from DTV vector and information of peaks and valleys from DTV curves" (Sec. 2)
notes: Judgment call: DTV from the 2C CC charge (Oxford charges from the discharged state); SVD of the whole DTV vector over the full CC charge -> P2c=yes [P2c_basis=whole-curve DTV]. Whether the LSTM input sequence includes past SOH values and how cells are split is not stated. Joint SOH/RUL paper; included because current SOH estimation is reported.

title: A Method for Estimating the SOH of Lithium-Ion Batteries Based on Graph Perceptual Neural Network
datasets: Sandia National Laboratories (NCA, NMC, LFP; 100% DOD) and Toyota Research Institute/MIT LFP
inputs: 20 features from current, voltage, voltage-capacity and temperature data incl. charging time, discharging time, coulomb count during charging and discharging, CV charging time, slopes, averages; graph-aware (GPNN) network with random feature elimination
evidence: P1/P2: "coulomb count (during charging and discharging)"; "charging time, discharging time" (Sec. 2.3)
notes: Sandia cells cycled at 100% DOD, so charge coulomb count and discharge time span the full cycle (capacity-equivalent). Final retained subset after random feature elimination not reported in extracted text; coding applies to the proposed feature pool. Train/test split not stated. Comparisons only vs DL models.

title: Integrated Mixed Attention U-Net Mechanisms with Multi-Stage Division Strategy Customized for Accurate Estimation of Lithium-Ion Battery State of Health
datasets: XJTU battery dataset (batches 1-3)
inputs: V, I, T sequences from the discharge process -> SOH sequence; mixed-attention U-Net with multi-stage (knee-point) division of the degradation curve
notes: Stages are defined by geometric knee points of each battery's full capacity-degradation curve ("Stage division" precedes train/test in pipeline); the text does not say how a test battery's stage is assigned -> P3 unclear (possible whole-life leakage). Input coverage of the discharge (full vs partial) not stated. Leave-one-battery-out validation.

title: Physical Information-Guided Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks for Battery State of Health Estimation
datasets: Toyota Research Institute (MIT/Severson) 124 LFP cells
inputs: Full 4C discharge voltage and temperature curves interpolated to 1024 points with original discharge time tau preserved, plus normalized cycle index; KAN-PINN with Verhulst constraint
evidence: P2: "With the original discharge time tau preserved, both voltage and temperature profiles are interpolated" (Sec. 2)
notes: Discharge time under 4C CC to cutoff = Q/I -> capacity-equivalent input. "Cycle numbers are normalized to facilitate cross-sample comparison" -> normalization reference (per-cell life vs global) not stated -> P3 unclear. Split 41/40/43 cells. Comparisons only vs DL models.

title: State of Health Estimation Method for Lithium-Ion Batteries via Generalized Additivity Model and Transfer Component Analysis
datasets: Oxford Battery Degradation Dataset 1
inputs: Sampled values of a segment of the IC curve (CC charge), transfer component analysis, generalized additive model (GAM)
notes: Partial IC segment. Train on cell 8, test on other cells (TCA uses unlabeled target features). Linear regression, SVR, NN, CNN trained on traditional IC features for comparison.
